findings.evidence: All 56 keys are option "a" (56/56). Any learner who always picks "a" scores 100%. Also the key is the longest option in 33/56 items (59% vs 25% chance) and is usually a near-verbatim lift of the passage while distractors are off-topic (e.g. "Economic benefits of learning global languages").
findings.suggestion: Randomise key position (target ~25% each of a-d), rebalance option length, and make distractors plausible misreadings of the passage. Check the builder (build-reading-track.mjs) for a fixed-position option array.

findings.evidence: All 56 items have difficulty 3 and expectedSeconds 60, including 1-line vocabulary items (hum1-q5 merely=simply) and the two-passage synthesis items (aca2-q5). roles core/challenge/variant carry no difficulty signal; challenge q5 is equal to or easier than core.
findings.suggestion: Assign graded difficulty (e.g. vocab 2, detail 2-3, inference/synthesis 4) and varied expectedSeconds; make challenge items genuinely harder.

findings.evidence: Every passage is 30-39 words (2 sentences) and is re-used verbatim for all 7 questions of the lesson (8 passages total). catalog "example" is the same text. Not a reading passage of the length used in Korean 수능/내신 or in B1-B2 reading tasks (~120-300 words). Register is C1/academic-jargon (token sequences, intentionality, salience, neoclassical, decouple, anomalies), above the CEFR B1-B2 claimed in scripts/learn/reading/lessons.mjs header, and the sentences read as written-for-test summaries rather than authentic text.
findings.suggestion: Replace with 120-250 word passages (distinct per lesson or per question group), and state the actual CEFR band (likely B2-C1) or simplify. Do not claim authenticity unless sourced; note no native/teacher review is claimed.

findings.evidence: 7 questions per lesson on a 2-sentence passage forces near-duplicates, e.g. hum1 q1 (theme), q3 (what is lost), q4 (statement consistent), q6 (role of memory) all test "language carries cultural memory/values; losing it is a loss".
findings.suggestion: Cut redundant items or move to longer passages with distinct targets (detail, inference, vocabulary, structure).

findings.evidence: Catalog lists only q1-q4 (questionIds) + q5 (challengeId) per lesson; 16 questions (q6 and q7 of every lesson: hum1/hum2/sci1/sci2/eco1/eco2/aca1/aca2) are not referenced by any lesson. So "56 questions" is 40 reachable via catalog (+16 orphan variants).
findings.suggestion: Confirm the variant pool is intentionally used by the app (e.g. family/role variants); otherwise reference them or report 40.

findings.evidence: Neither catalog nor any lesson/question cites an achievement-standard code (no "12영", no "standards" field; only "curriculum":"life-help-english-reading-v1"). Course ids/titles do not map to a 2022 course name. Course titles also overreach: "학술 논리와 빈칸 추론" contains no blank-inference item.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit standard codes per lesson (see courses[].standards) and, ideally, a course mapping to 영어 독해와 작문 / 심화 영어 독해와 작문.

findings.question: en-el-aca1-q1
findings.evidence: Lesson title "논리적 전제와 빈칸 추론" and catalog tagline "숨은 전제 찾기, 빈칸 추론" but none of the 7 aca1 questions is a blank-completion or hidden-premise item; they are detail/vocabulary/stance questions. aca1 concept "논리적 전제 분석 기법" is not trained.
findings.suggestion: Add real 빈칸 추론 (gap in passage, choose logical completion) and 숨은 전제 items, or rename the lesson.

findings.question: en-el-aca2-q1
findings.evidence: "Two-passage integration" is a single 36-word text containing two one-sentence summaries ("Passage A argues... Passage B contends..."). No actual Passage A/B, so comparison/synthesis (aca2-q1,q3,q5,q7) relies on stated positions, not reading. Passage B overgeneralises ("always yield ... cannot be anticipated"), a strawman.
findings.suggestion: Provide two real short passages (80-150 words each) with arguments and evidence.

findings.question: en-el-aca2-q5
findings.evidence: Key "Short-term disruption requires support while preparing for novel cognitive roles" introduces a normative claim (support/policy) that neither summary states, so it is not entailed by the text; it is only the least absurd option (others: "outlawed", "abandon all education").
findings.suggestion: Rewrite stem/key so the conclusion follows from A+B (e.g. "Both ... transitions are disruptive but may create new roles") and make distractors plausible partial syntheses (only-A, only-B).

findings.question: en-el-aca2-q1
findings.evidence: A claims speed ("faster than new industries can generate replacement roles"), not that net employment ultimately falls; B claims eventual creation. Key says "ultimately creates more employment than it displaces", slightly misframing the A/B disagreement (speed/timing vs eventual outcome). Still the only reasonable option.
findings.suggestion: Reword: "whether new jobs appear fast enough to replace those lost".

findings.question: en-el-aca1-q6
findings.evidence: Asks for the view "most consistent with the author", key "Thomas Kuhn's paradigm shift model" requires outside knowledge and a named thinker absent from the passage; passage is a paraphrase of Kuhn, so effectively a trivia/giveaway item (distractors: "Ancient scholastic authoritarianism", "Purely mechanical linear positivism"). Hint/explanation consistent with the key but both rely on Kuhn.
findings.suggestion: Replace with a text-based inference, or supply Kuhn in the passage.

findings.question: en-el-aca1-q1
findings.evidence: aca1 q1 (driver of progress = revolutionary reorganisation when anomalies persist) and q3 (trigger = persistent anomalies paradigms cannot resolve) and q4 (rejects steady accumulation) test the same sentence; keys are near-identical restatements.
findings.suggestion: Merge or replace with distinct skills.

findings.question: en-el-hum2-q7
findings.evidence: Stem "글쓴이가 배격하는 가설" - key (decisions affect only the actor) is supported by "rarely affect only the decision-maker", fine, but "rarely" is weaker than "reject"; low risk. Options b-d are trivially false.
findings.suggestion: Optional wording tweak ("반박하는 통념").

findings.question: en-el-sci1-q1
findings.evidence: Passage asserts as fact that generative models "do not possess subjective experience or intentionality" and that statistical processing "cannot replicate" embodied comprehension - contested philosophy-of-mind positions stated without attribution/hedge; questions q1,q5,q7 then treat them as facts. "Token sequences/corpora" is technical jargon.
findings.suggestion: Attribute the claim ("Some researchers argue...") and phrase questions "according to the author".

findings.question: en-el-sci1-q6
findings.evidence: Distractors "mathematically identical", "purely accidental", "invisible and hidden" are not plausible; "noticeable and important" is also correct only in the psychology sense, passage gives no gloss.
findings.suggestion: Add plausible distractors (e.g. "emotionally overwhelming").

findings.question: en-el-sci2-q2
findings.evidence: Explanation glosses incremental as "점진적인, 미미한 증가의" ("미미한" = negligible) but key says "gradual and small in scale" - acceptable; the Korean "미미한 증가" overstates smallness. Also sci2 q2/q5/q7 test "incrementalism" three times.
findings.suggestion: Drop "미미한"; dedupe.

findings.question: en-el-sci2-q1
findings.evidence: Lesson title "기후 회복력과 청정 기술" (resilience/clean tech) but passage is about climate mitigation, circular economy and decoupling energy from fossil fuels; "resilience/adaptation" is absent.
findings.suggestion: Retitle (e.g. 기후 위기 완화와 순환경제).

findings.question: en-el-sci2-q3
findings.evidence: Passage claims materials are "endlessly repurposed" and grids "decouple entirely" from fossil fuels - absolute claims (not thermodynamically/practically achievable); the stems treat them as required ("완전히 분리되어야"). Not factually sound as a policy statement.
findings.suggestion: Hedge ("largely", "increasingly").

findings.question: en-el-eco1-q4
findings.evidence: Key "feel the pain of loss more acutely than joy of gain" vs q2 key "Weighing losses much more heavily than equal gains": same concept twice (q2/q4 duplicate). Option d "systematically double the value of positive gains" is an inaccurate parody.
findings.suggestion: Replace q4 with an inference item.

findings.question: en-el-eco1-q1
findings.evidence: Lesson concept mentions "의사결정 프레이밍" (framing) but passage covers only rationality vs loss aversion; framing never appears.
findings.suggestion: Remove "프레이밍" or add framing text.

findings.question: en-el-eco2-q1
findings.evidence: Concept claims "국경 없는 데이터 흐름과 글로벌 공급망의 구조적 변화" but passage has neither data flows nor supply chains. Passage claim that micro-enterprises "access worldwide capital markets" is overstated/unsupported; q2 key adds "customer markets" not in text.
findings.suggestion: Align concept to passage; hedge claim ("access global customers and funding platforms").

findings.question: en-el-eco2-q7
findings.evidence: eco2 q1 (what distinguishes modern globalization) and q7 (central topic: transformation through digital platforms) have near-identical keys; q5 is also the first sentence. Also "decouple" vocabulary is tested in sci2-q6 and eco2-q6 (and appears in the sci2/eco2 passages), a repeated word across courses.
findings.suggestion: Dedupe; vary vocabulary targets.

findings.question: en-el-hum1-q7
findings.evidence: Tone question key "appreciative and concerned" vs distractors "optimistic and dismissive/indifferent and neutral" - passage is expository, tone item has weak evidence; solvable only by elimination.
findings.suggestion: Use a text-evidence item.

findings.question: en-el-sci2-q7
findings.evidence: Title/conclusion item whose distractors are absurd extremes ("The Impossibility of Clean Energy Grids", "Why Fossil Fuels Are Permanently Essential", "AI will completely replace all human thought within a decade") - extreme words make the key obvious without comprehension.
findings.suggestion: Use moderate distractors that over/under-generalise.
